road.name: The Toll of Empty Wagons
road.threat: Armed extortion and a trapped causeway. A rope or climbing kit can open a side approach.
road.brief: Three wagons carrying winter seed have stopped answering their road signals. Find the missing drivers before the village’s planting stores are sold across the border.
road.opening: An abandoned wagon stands with its wheels chocked, not broken. From the tollhouse beyond, a bell repeats three short notes. A driver behind a shutter flashes a hand and vanishes.
road.clue: The road signal has been reversed. Drivers are being held while their cargo is inventoried; the toll captain’s own payment slips contradict his orders.

investigate.label: Compare the wagon manifest with the toll notices
investigate.success: You find two incompatible seals. The captain has been collecting an illegal second toll and hiding the drivers who objected.
investigate.failure: The handwriting defeats you, but you find a driver’s scratched tally: the prisoners are still alive. You now know where to focus.

route.label: Cross under the causeway and reach the drivers
route.success: You cross beneath the sentries. The prisoners pass you a complete set of duplicate receipts.
route.failure: A loose stone gives you away. You reach the tollhouse, but the captain pulls his guards inward.

crisis.narrate: Captain Venn offers to release the wagons if you leave the documents. The drivers watch his hands; one rests on a signal cord leading toward their locked yard.
Captain Venn offers to release the wagons if you turn round now and forget you ever saw his yard. The drivers watch his hands; one rests on a signal cord leading toward their locked yard.

peaceful.label: Use the duplicate receipts to make the guards stand down

success.narrate: The guards read what they have been paid to enforce. One cuts the yard lock; the captain surrenders his keys without a fight.

You don't have the captain's papers, so you ask the drivers instead, loudly, in front of his guards: how long they have been held, what has been taken off their carts, and who signed for it. The guards have families on this road too. By the third answer one of them cuts the yard lock, and the captain surrenders his keys without a fight.

peaceful.failure: Venn calls the receipts stolen and signals the yard guard. His hesitation gives you a chance to reach the lock before the drivers are moved.
peaceful.labelNoLead: Ask the drivers, in front of the guards, what they are being held for

objective.name: Release the wagon drivers
objective.label: Break the yard lock
objective.description: Two successful actions release the drivers and end the encounter without needing to defeat every guard.
objective.failText: Venn moves part of the stolen cargo. The seed shortage will persist, and the drivers still need a way out.
objective.successText: The drivers escape with their wagons; the remaining guards abandon the tollhouse.

road.after: The drivers recover their animals. The confiscated coin could compensate the households at once or fund an escort for future caravans.

decisions.label: Return the illegal tolls to the drivers
decisions.text: Families recover their winter coin. Briarwatch’s trust in you grows.

decisions.label: Fund a permanent caravan escort
decisions.text: Iona receives enough money to keep a watch on the road. Trading houses recognize your work.

road.approach: The causeway runs straight at the tollhouse, in full view of its shutters. Underneath it, the old drainage arches lead toward the drivers’ yard: low, wet and out of sight.

marsh.name: Bitter Water at Fenmere
marsh.threat: Poisonous vapor and flooded paths. Antitoxin protects the next poison save; a lantern helps identify safe valves.
marsh.brief: Fenmere’s well has turned bitter. The village blames marsh gatherers, who in turn blame a new pumping station. Find the cause before fear becomes violence.
marsh.opening: Reeds lie flat around the pumping station. A sick heron watches from a dry pipe. On opposite banks, villagers and gatherers wait with improvised weapons.
marsh.clue: The pump carries dissolved ward ash upstream. Both communities drink the same tainted water; neither poisoned the other.

investigate.label: Examine the pump residue with the gathered healers
investigate.success: The copper-green residue is artificial. You trace it to a cracked containment jar feeding the intake.
investigate.failure: Your samples are spoiled, but the sick fish cluster below the new pump. It is enough to turn suspicion toward the machinery.

route.label: Reach the intake through the vapor trench
route.success: You choose the dry stepping stones and arrive without disturbing the trapped vapor.
route.failure: A gas pocket ruptures around the party. You reach the intake coughing, with less time to work.

marsh.crisis: A bound marsh guardian lashes at anyone near the valves. Its keeper shouts that opening the spillway will flood the gatherers’ shelters; leaving it shut will poison the well again.

peaceful.label: Show both banks the residue and organize a controlled release
peaceful.success: Both groups carry their vulnerable neighbors to high ground. With no one left in its threatened boundary, the guardian accepts the keeper’s recall.
peaceful.failure: The warning gets some people moving, but the keeper cannot calm the guardian. You must open the safe valves while it rages.
peaceful.labelNoLead: Get both banks to look at the water together and organize a controlled release

objective.name: Vent the poisoned intake
objective.label: Turn a safe intake valve
objective.description: Three successful actions purge the poison and release the guardian. Antitoxin protects against the trench, not physical attacks.
objective.failText: The emergency spill floods some shelters. Stop the danger to prevent further losses; the flooded homes will need repair.
objective.successText: Clean water replaces the bitter flow; the guardian’s bindings dissolve.

marsh.after: With clean water running, the two banks must decide who will care for the pump. Neither trusts the other yet.

decisions.label: Establish a shared water council
decisions.text: Each bank appoints a keeper. It is slower work, but neither controls the other’s drinking water.

decisions.label: Ask Ashford’s engineers to maintain the pump
decisions.text: Paid engineers take charge and guarantee a regular inspection schedule.

marsh.approach: A trench of yellow vapor runs under the reeds to the intake. The causeway above it is dry and open, and both banks are watching it.

bridge.name: The Last Cart over Ashford
bridge.threat: Sabotaged anchors and barricades. Climbing gear helps cross; protecting refugees matters more than chasing every raider.
bridge.brief: Refugees are trapped beyond the western bridge. Orin recognizes the banners of the company holding it. Get the last carts across before a demolition charge is lit.
bridge.opening: A bridge bell sounds once for each cart allowed through. The queue stopped an hour ago. Under the span, freshly cut cables sway over the river.
bridge.clue: The demolition order is forged. A faction within the bridge company intends to abandon both refugees and its own rear guard.

investigate.label: Ask the bridge veterans to compare their orders
investigate.success: Orin points out a commander’s signature from a man who died years ago. Several soldiers realize they were meant to be expendable.
investigate.failure: The veterans close ranks. One quietly warns you that the demolition fuse is already laid beneath the guardhouse.

route.label: Cross the maintenance anchors to the far gate
route.success: You reach the fuse box unseen and disconnect the first charge.
route.failure: An anchor tears loose. You reach the far bank bruised, while the sentries call their lieutenant.

bridge.crisis: Lieutenant Hal says her orders allow no exceptions. Behind her, a child in the last cart asks Orin whether soldiers always leave first.

peaceful.label: Offer the soldiers a shared withdrawal with the refugees
peaceful.success: Hal orders every cart onto the bridge, then marches her company out behind them. No one is left as a diversion.
peaceful.failure: Most soldiers hesitate, but the demolition crew follows its own orders. You must clear the cart route under fire.

objective.name: Escort the final refugee carts
objective.label: Open a lane for a refugee cart
objective.description: Three successful actions secure the evacuation. Companions hold the demolition crew away from you.
objective.failText: One loaded supply cart is lost to the river. The remaining people still need a crossing, and Highpass will receive fewer blankets and tools.
objective.successText: The last cart reaches the near bank; the demolition crew has nothing left to hold hostage.

bridge.after: The bridge is safe for now. Hal asks whether you will make an example of the confused soldiers or let them help repair what they nearly destroyed.

decisions.label: Offer supervised repair work instead of punishment
decisions.text: The company works beside the refugees. Orin recognizes a way to make his old failure count for something.

decisions.label: Preserve the orders and call a public tribunal
decisions.text: The forged orders enter the public record. Ashford’s council must answer for the chain of command.

bridge.approach: The maintenance anchors hang under the span, slick with river spray. On the deck above, the queue of carts waits in plain sight of Hal’s line.

archive.name: Letters from the Drowned Archive
archive.threat: Rising water, undead wardens and fragile records. A lantern helps navigation; holy water or radiant weapons affect the undead.
archive.brief: Maren’s missing shrine keepers sent their last letters here. Find the archive’s ward diagram and recover what remains before the reservoir rises again.
archive.opening: Desks drift at the foot of a flooded stair. Above them, a spectral archivist keeps sorting ruined pages into dry drawers that no longer exist.
archive.clue: The ward network was built as a council of independent voices. A single central command would bind every keeper as Sable tried to bind the bell spirit.

investigate.label: Read the surviving correspondence with Maren
investigate.success: Maren reads the names aloud. The letters reveal both the network’s design and the location of its missing keystone.
investigate.failure: Most ink is gone, but Maren identifies the final dispatch mark: all roads in the correspondence lead to Highpass.

route.label: Navigate the flooded stacks without breaking the seals
route.success: You find a service stair and preserve the dry alcoves along the route.
route.failure: A shelf collapses beneath you. You reach the central record chamber with water rising behind your boots.

archive.crisis: The archivist will not release the ward diagram until every keeper has been accounted for. Some never returned. Destroying it would be easier than admitting the truth.

peaceful.label: Read the keepers’ names and acknowledge the unfinished record
peaceful.success: The archivist stops sorting. It gathers the last letters from the one dry drawer and holds them out, not to you, but to Maren. Then it opens the diagram cabinet and lets the party pass.
peaceful.failure: The unfinished names catch in the ward. The archivist turns hostile, but the cabinet remains close enough to reach.

objective.name: Recover the diagram and last letters
objective.label: Preserve a sealed record drawer
objective.description: Three successful actions recover the essential records and end the binding. Killing enemies is not required.
objective.failText: Some personal letters dissolve before they can be sealed. The diagram and remaining names still need to be recovered.
objective.successText: The sealed drawers float free; the archivist is released from its impossible duty.

after.narrate: The diagram is safe in its oilcloth. Maren has the keepers’ letters, a damp bundle tied with archive string, and she has stopped at the one on top.

after.text: Brother Edric Moss. He kept the well-ward at Fenmere. To his sister Hesper, at the dyers’ yard in Highpass.
You knew him.
He owed me two candles and an apology. He would have paid the candles.

after.narrate: She puts the letter inside her coat, next to her list.
The diagram could be published for everyone who tends a ward, or kept under council protection while the sabotage is investigated.

decisions.label: Share the diagram with local ward keepers
decisions.text: Knowledge spreads beyond a single council. The keepers can prepare their own defenses.

decisions.label: Give the original to a guarded public archive
decisions.text: The council establishes a protected record, with named witnesses for every copy.

archive.approach: The flooded stacks run in long aisles toward the record chamber. Some shelves still hold their seals, and one wrong step brings a whole wall of them down. The main stair is clear, loud, and in full view.

signal.name: A Light above the Storm
signal.threat: Charged ward machinery and exposed climbing. A Storm Grounder opens a protected approach; a climbing kit aids the ascent.
signal.brief: The tower above Highpass repeats a distress signal in Nessa’s old code. Restore its beacon before the mountain caravans enter the storm blind.
signal.opening: Lightning crawls sideways across the tower’s bronze rings. Someone has tied a scout’s scarf around the lowest signal arm, where it cannot be seen from the road.
signal.clue: The tower is broadcasting a warning, not summoning the storm. Its keeper diverted the lightning to prevent a central command from taking control.

investigate.label: Decode the interrupted signal sequence

success.narrate: Nessa recognizes her mentor’s shorthand. The last message names the keystone’s carrier and an unguarded path to the summit.
The log is in a keeper’s private shorthand, and it takes you most of an hour with the station’s codebook. The last message names the keystone’s carrier and an unguarded path to the summit.

investigate.failure: The sequence is broken, but you identify the distress cadence. Someone tried to keep the tower independent.

route.label: Climb beneath the charged signal rings
route.success: You earth the nearest ring and reach the control platform through a quiet pocket in the storm.
route.failure: The rings arc across your route. You reach the platform, but the tower’s bound sentinels awaken.

signal.crisis: The keeper lies under a fallen signal arm, still shielding the manual release. A storm sentinel orders you to surrender the beacon to the central ward command.

peaceful.label: Transmit the keeper’s independent recall sequence
peaceful.success: The sentinel accepts the local keeper’s authority. It braces the arm while you pull the keeper clear and restore the beacon.
peaceful.failure: The sentinel recognizes only part of the code. It hesitates long enough for you to reach the manual releases.
peaceful.labelNoLead: Help the trapped keeper send her own recall signal

objective.name: Restore the beacon and free the keeper
objective.label: Reset a beacon release
objective.description: Three successful actions end the encounter. The Storm Grounder also helps these objective checks.
objective.failText: The beacon loses its long-range lens. The keeper still needs release, and some caravans will have to wait for daylight.
objective.successText: The beacon turns toward the road; the keeper’s warning reaches Highpass.

after.narrate: Highpass’s medics carry the keeper down on a door. Her leg is wrong below the knee, and she gives instructions about the beacon the whole way.

after.text: You tied your scarf to the wrong arm. Nobody could see it from the road.
I didn’t tie it. You did. I came because I saw it.
Then I tied it to the wrong arm.

after.narrate: She pushes a folded map into Nessa’s hands: every safe line through the pass, redrawn after each storm for twenty years.

after.text: Reliable as of this morning. After that, it’s yours to keep honest.
I’ll bring it back to you.
Bring it back better.

after.narrate: Before the medics take her down, the keeper, Wren, presses a folded map on you: every safe line through the pass, redrawn after each storm for twenty years. “Give it to someone who’ll keep it honest.”
Highpass asks which travelers should receive the first safe signal windows.

decisions.label: Prioritize the refugee and healer caravans
decisions.text: The most vulnerable travelers reach shelter first. The outpost’s trust grows.

decisions.label: Prioritize supply trains for the whole pass
decisions.text: Food and repair equipment arrive before the next storm front.

signal.approach: The charged rings turn above the climb, throwing sparks onto the rock. The tower’s front stair is open and lit, and every sentinel on the platform can see it.

summit.name: The Price of a Keystone
summit.threat: Rival claimants, fragile bridges and exposed negotiations. Climbing gear helps travel; information and reputation may prevent a fight.
summit.brief: A courier carries the ward keystone toward Glasswind. Three factions have promised to protect the region if you hand it to them. Find the courier and decide who can be trusted with power.
summit.opening: Three camps share a ledge too narrow for a battle. The courier sits between them, protecting a wrapped object while representatives argue over whose banner it belongs beneath.
summit.clue: Each claimant has omitted a condition from its offer. The courier’s oath permits a shared custody agreement witnessed by independent ward keepers.

investigate.label: Compare all three custody agreements
investigate.success: You expose the missing clauses without humiliating their authors. A common agreement becomes possible.
investigate.failure: The promises blur together, but the courier points to the part none of them read aloud: custody can be shared.

route.label: Secure a neutral meeting place beyond the cracked bridge
route.success: You establish a safe crossing and invite one witness from each camp.
route.failure: A support cracks during the crossing. No one is lost, but accusations fly and hired guards draw weapons.

summit.crisis: An agent of the central command offers to end the argument by binding the keystone to one keeper. The courier refuses, and the agent reaches for the wrapped stone.

peaceful.label: Bind the claimants to a witnessed shared-custody oath
peaceful.success: Each representative signs in front of their own people. The agent loses the authority it used to demand obedience.
peaceful.failure: Two representatives agree; the third panics as the agent seizes a witness. You must break the coercive seals before anyone is bound.

objective.name: Break the coercive custody seals
objective.label: Release a witness from a binding seal
objective.description: Three successful actions free the witnesses and secure the keystone. Companions cannot negotiate these releases for the hero.
objective.failText: One representative loses trust during the delay. The keystone still needs securing; any custody agreement will begin under strain.
objective.successText: The witnesses stand together and the agent’s seals fall apart.

summit.after: The keystone is yours to carry, but not necessarily yours to own. Its custody will shape who answers the final beacon.

decisions.label: Keep custody shared among the local wards
decisions.text: The local keepers trust you to carry the keystone without claiming it.

decisions.label: Place custody with an accountable regional council
decisions.text: The council names witnesses and accepts public responsibility for the stone.

summit.approach: A cracked footbridge leads round to a neutral ledge above the three camps. The main path runs straight through all of them, past every banner.

breach.name: The Quiet District
breach.threat: Sleep-binding constructs and sealed evacuation gates. Ward oil and tools help, but choosing an evacuation route matters most.
breach.brief: An entire district has stopped sending messengers. Its residents still move through familiar routines, but none can choose to leave. Break the command relays without turning the streets into a battlefield.
breach.opening: A baker kneads the same empty board. A child opens and closes a school gate. Every movement pauses when the bell in the central square clicks rather than rings.
breach.clue: The relays use remembered routines to replace decisions. Interrupting their shared rhythm will release the residents without damaging the wards that keep them safe.

investigate.label: Find the break between remembered routine and living choice
investigate.success: You ask a resident a question with no familiar answer. For a moment they wake and point out the three relay anchors.
investigate.failure: Your questions fail to wake anyone, but Maren notices that their pauses do not align with the street clock. The command is external.

route.label: Reach the relays through the service courtyards
route.success: The routines conceal your movement. You wedge the evacuation gate before the relay notices.
route.failure: A service door rings against a guard’s route. Sentinels arrive, but the evacuation gate is within reach.

breach.crisis: The district’s bound magistrate begs you not to destroy the protective wards. The command construct uses her voice to order the sentinels to keep everyone safely inside.

peaceful.label: Give the residents a new, voluntary signal to follow
peaceful.success: An unfamiliar song moves from window to window. The residents choose to answer it; the command loses its borrowed voices.
peaceful.failure: A few residents wake, enough to begin an evacuation. The construct tightens its remaining hold and sends the sentinels after you.

objective.name: Disconnect the command without destroying the wards
objective.label: Free a command relay
objective.description: Four successful actions release the district. Complete the objective before round seven to preserve all three local wards.
objective.failText: The emergency mechanism burns out one local ward. The residents still need release, and later repairs will be unavoidable.
objective.successText: The last relay goes quiet. People begin making small, uncertain choices of their own.

breach.after: The magistrate asks who should decide when a ward may override a person’s wishes. The answer will travel with you to the final beacon.

decisions.label: Require the keeper’s and community’s consent
decisions.text: The district adopts a double-consent rule. Independence now has a practical safeguard.

decisions.label: Create a public emergency oversight council
decisions.text: Emergency powers require named, reviewable votes and a fixed expiry.

breach.approach: The service courtyards run behind the bakery and the school, where the routines are loudest. The main street is empty, clicking, and watched by the relay sentinels.

beacon.name: The Chorus at Dawn
beacon.threat: A command engine protected by bound echoes. The keystone, your allies, and the decisions recorded on the road determine how it can be stopped.
beacon.brief: The central command is preparing its final signal. Carry the keystone to the first beacon and decide whether the ward network will become a shield shared by many or a command held by one.
beacon.opening: The first beacon stands above the cloud line. Voices from the towns you visited echo through its open rings, each clipped into a single obedient note.
beacon.clue: The command has no voice of its own. It can be severed by making the wards answer independently, or destroyed at the cost of burning the central lens.

investigate.label: Listen for the separate voices beneath the command
investigate.success: You recognize the people behind the notes. Their choices along the road give you a sequence the command cannot predict.
investigate.failure: The chorus overwhelms you, but your companions each find one familiar voice. You can still reach the keystone cradle.

route.label: Carry the keystone through the resonant rings
route.success: You ground the nearest rings and reach the cradle before the command finishes tuning them.
route.failure: A peal throws the party against the stone. The cradle remains reachable, but the bound echoes gather around it.

crisis.narrate: The rings close into one note, and the note finds words. The voice is a man’s: tired, patient, and very reasonable.

crisis.text: High Warden Corvane, Central Command. You have walked a long way to break the only thing that has ever kept the Gloam out of a nursery.

I have watched councils. I watched one argue about whose turn it was to ring the bell while the mist came over the wall. The vote was still open when the last house went quiet. The design you are standing in was drawn by someone who saw that. She wanted a voice that could answer before the arguing finished. So do I.
And who does the voice answer to?
Nobody needs to. That is the point, Stoneward.
He believes it. Every word.

crisis.narrate: The Single Voice offers perfect safety at the cost of every keeper’s choice. It sounds less convincing now that you have seen whom such safety leaves behind.

peaceful.label: Ask the independent keepers to answer together
peaceful.success: The keepers answer in different rhythms. The command cannot make them agree without choosing for them; its central note falls apart.
peaceful.failure: The first voices answer, then falter under the pressure. Your companions hold the echoes back while you open the remaining channels.

objective.name: Restore a chorus of independent wards
objective.label: Open an independent ward channel
objective.description: Four successful actions sever the command. Your earlier community decisions lower the difficulty; the change is shown before rolling.
objective.failText: The central lens cracks while the command continues. Break the command to free the roads; rebuilding the lens will take longer.
objective.successText: Separate voices fill the rings. The region’s wards become a chorus, not a chain.

beacon.after: Dawn reaches the roads below. Your party has earned the right to define what its strength is for. The guild has prepared the first advancement trial—not as a reward for obedience, but as a question.

decisions.label: Leave the wards in independent, cooperating hands
decisions.text: Every settlement keeps its own voice. Your party becomes a link between them, not a ruler above them.

decisions.label: Found a public charter for the ward network
decisions.text: A shared charter limits the network’s power and names the people who must answer for its use.

beacon.approach: The rings hum between you and the keystone cradle, close enough to feel in your teeth. The pilgrims’ stair goes straight up the middle, where the command will hear every step.

trial.name: Oath of the Road — First Advancement
trial.threat: A supervised trial of judgment and technique. Failure has no gold penalty and can be retried; your class mastery cannot be lost to one bad roll.
trial.brief: Show how you use your strength when victory and protection compete. Complete this trial to earn your class mastery. Your next branch, your second job, is chosen at level 20.
trial.opening: The trainers create an echo of the road you have traveled. Your companions stand beside you; behind a fragile gate, voices ask whether your next step will leave them behind.
trial.clue: The trial’s gate responds to commitment, not brute force. A deliberate choice of responsibility can resolve the echo without defeating it.

investigate.label: Discuss what the road taught you with your companions

success.narrate: The trainers dim the echo and leave you the bench by the gate. Nobody hurries you.

success.text: At Ashford you let the bridge crews work off what they owed instead of hanging it on them. I wanted a tribunal. I was wrong, and the bridge got mended in half the time.
At Ashford you kept Hal’s orders and called a tribunal. Slow. But every carter on that bridge watched it happen, and none of them had to take our word for anything.
You gave the diagram to every keeper who asked. Some of them will use it badly. All of them can use it.
You put the diagram where it could be watched, with a name beside every copy. I wrote the names down too. Habit.
Highpass. You sent the refugee carts through first, and the supply train sat in the snow a whole day. I counted the people on those carts. Forty-two.
Highpass. You sent the supply trains first. I was angry for a week. Then the pass had food all winter, and I stopped being angry and started being annoyed that you were right.

success.narrate: Each of them is holding a different day of the road. Between them, the trial’s question gets smaller and sharper: not what you can do, but who you do it for.

failure.narrate: The trainers leave you the bench by the gate. It goes badly.

failure.text: The Quiet District. Double consent. If a ward has to ask twice before it saves someone, someone drowns while it’s asking.
And if it never has to ask, you get a street full of bakers kneading empty boards.
It isn’t meant to be fair. It’s meant to be true.
The oversight council. Named votes, a fixed expiry. I like it. I like anything with an expiry.
You like it because it sounds like a duty roster. Councils lie in ways a roster can’t.
Every council I have ever sat on.

failure.narrate: Nobody wins. But by the end you know what each of them is afraid you might become, and that is its own kind of answer.

route.label: Demonstrate your class technique on the approach
route.success: The trainers recognize a practiced technique used for a purpose. The gate responds.
route.failure: The technique falters, and a trainer resets the echo. You learn from the miss and proceed without losing your path.

trial.crisis: The echo offers an easy victory while the gate behind it cracks. The trainers watch whether you pursue the enemy or take responsibility for the people in your care.

peaceful.label: Name your responsibility and let the easy victory go
peaceful.success: You refuse the false choice. The echo bows and the gate opens; the trial recognizes your judgment.
peaceful.failure: The words are not enough. The trainers ask you to show the decision while the echo presses its attack.

objective.name: Demonstrate responsibility under pressure
objective.label: Secure the trial gate
objective.description: Three successful actions complete the demonstration. A failed trial is recoverable and cannot permanently lock an advancement.
objective.failText: The trainers mark the missed deadline for discussion. Finish the demonstration or withdraw and retry; your advancement cannot be permanently lost.
objective.successText: The gate holds. The trainers acknowledge the intent behind your technique.

after.narrate: The echo is gone. The gate is still standing, and so are the people behind it. The trainers wait with the guild’s book open. The Oath of the Road is one sentence long, and they will not say it for you.

after.text: They want it out loud. I said mine to a sergeant with a head cold. Don’t overthink it.
Overthink it a little. Then mean it.
Or say it fast, before you can change your mind. That’s what I’d do.
That is what you’d do.

decisions.label: Swear the Oath of the Road: for the people who cannot hold the road themselves
decisions.description: Speak your oath. The guild records it, and the road remembers it. Every oath earns the same class mastery.

text.narrate: “I will hold the road for the people who cannot hold it themselves, and I will not leave them behind to win.”

text.text: Good.

text.narrate: The guild writes it down. Your second job is chosen at level 20. A relief convoy is stuck on the Highpass road and needs you now; the practice arena stays open for safe experiments.

decisions.label: Swear the Oath of the Road: for the ones who walk it with you
decisions.description: Speak your oath. The guild records it, and the road remembers it. Every oath earns the same class mastery.

text.narrate: “I will walk the road with the people beside me, and I will not ask them to go where I will not.”

text.text: You already don’t. You just never said it.

text.narrate: The guild writes it down. Your second job is chosen at level 20. A relief convoy is stuck on the Highpass road and needs you now; the practice arena stays open for safe experiments.

decisions.label: Swear the Oath of the Road: for the towns, even when they cannot agree
decisions.description: Speak your oath. The guild records it, and the road remembers it. Every oath earns the same class mastery.

text.narrate: “I will keep the road open for every town on it, and I will not choose which of them is worth saving.”

text.text: Even Fenmere?

text.narrate: “Especially Fenmere.”
The guild writes it down. Your second job is chosen at level 20. A relief convoy is stuck on the Highpass road and needs you now; the practice arena stays open for safe experiments.

trial.approach: The trainers have laid out the echo’s road: a course built to show your technique, and beside it a plain path straight to the gate. Either is allowed. Both are watched.

aftermath.name: The Road You Keep
aftermath.threat: An isolated command engine is holding a relief caravan. Ward Oil can affect its guards; a climbing kit offers access to the emergency channel.
aftermath.brief: Take your new mastery onto the road. A surviving command engine has mistaken a relief convoy for an invading army; the first free towns need its medicine.
aftermath.opening: Children have painted the convoy’s crates with the symbols of their towns. Ahead, a gate of pale metal repeats an obsolete evacuation order. The driver has stopped arguing and started counting the sick.
aftermath.clue: The engine still accepts the old roadwardens’ responsibility oath. Its own emergency channel can release the gate without restoring the network’s central command.

investigate.label: Read the obsolete evacuation orders with the drivers
investigate.success: The contradictory commands reveal an emergency channel. It was designed for a keeper who would take personal responsibility for admitting the convoy.
investigate.failure: The exact wording is damaged, but the drivers remember a keeper’s oath. You know enough to challenge the command, though not how to make it easy.

route.label: Reach the emergency channel above the gate
route.success: The party reaches the channel before the guards can close the gallery. Your new training makes the opening feel usable, not merely lucky.
route.failure: A guard breaks the gallery brace. The party reaches the channel with injuries and without surprise.

aftermath.crisis: The engine asks who will answer for the people beyond its gate. Its guards advance. You may offer a binding promise, disable the engine, or work the channel while your companions keep the road open.

peaceful.label: Take responsibility for the convoy under the keepers’ oath

success.narrate: The engine asks for a keeper who will answer for the people beyond its gate. You have already sworn to something like that, out loud, in front of witnesses.
You give it the words you gave the guild: the people who cannot hold the road themselves.
You give it the words you gave the guild: the ones who walk the road with you, and the convoy is walking it now.
You give it the words you gave the guild: every town on the road, even the ones that cannot agree.
The engine accepts a responsible keeper in place of a distant master. It opens the gate and records the convoy’s destination, not its obedience.

peaceful.failure: The damaged engine refuses the oath. You must make room for the convoy before its guards enforce the old order.

objective.name: Open the relief convoy’s route
objective.label: Release an emergency road channel
objective.description: Four successful actions open the gate. Your new class mastery is among your combat actions: use it to buy whoever works the channel the time they need.
objective.failText: The convoy loses a day’s supply while it waits. Open the road to get the medicine through; the delay will be remembered.
objective.successText: The convoy passes between lowered weapons. People see what your new title means before anyone announces it.

aftermath.after: The convoy reaches the first settlement before dusk. Your mastery has faced something more demanding than a title ceremony: people depending on the way you choose to act.

decisions.label: Leave local keepers in charge of the road

text.narrate: The convoy appoints a keeper from each town. Your party leaves a working agreement rather than another command.

On the road home a rider in Highpass colours meets the convoy. The towns are sending delegates to Highpass, and the first council of the free wards sits at the end of the week. Captain Sorrel wants your party there. She did not say why, which from Sorrel means she expects trouble.

decisions.label: Found a voluntary road patrol with the companions

text.narrate: Your companions help volunteers agree on duties they can refuse or revise. The road belongs to those who keep it open.

On the road home a rider in Highpass colours meets the convoy. The towns are sending delegates to Highpass, and the first council of the free wards sits at the end of the week. Captain Sorrel wants your party there. She did not say why, which from Sorrel means she expects trouble.

approach.narrate: The emergency channel sits in a gallery above the gate, reached by a service ladder the guards have half pulled up. Below, the driver has laid the sick out in the shade of the crates, in order of who can wait least.

approach.text: Whatever you’re going to do, do it before the shade moves.

approach.narrate: Battle Surge is fresh in your arms. One breath of it would carry you up that ladder through a guard’s swing, and make your next blow land true.
Vanishing Step would put you in the gallery’s shadows before the guards had finished turning round.
An Arcane Barrier over whoever climbs first would let them take a guard’s blow and keep working.
Divine Aegis can keep whoever holds the channel on their feet while the guards try to drag them off it.
From the top of a crate, one Volley would reach every guard on the gallery at once.
Song of Rest will not open a gate, but it will keep the whole party standing while you do.

chairs.name: The Chair Problem
chairs.region: The officers' mess at Highpass Watch
chairs.threat: A council that cannot agree on its seating, and a Gloam front climbing the lower pass toward the refugee camp. Highpass's ward will only ring at full strength if the delegates agree to share its charge.
chairs.brief: The first council of the free wards sits at Highpass. Fenmere has sent for help. Get the towns to agree on anything before the mist does it for them.

opening.narrate: The first council of the free wards meets in the officers' mess at Highpass, because it is the only room in the fort with enough chairs. It does not have enough chairs.

opening.text: Six delegates. Five good chairs. One that rocks. I did the sum twice.

opening.narrate: Reeve Aveline has come for Briarwatch with a satchel of lists and the face of a woman who has not slept since the bell went quiet. Quartermaster Iona is here for Ashford, already reading the room's lease. A white-haired woman in a mud-stiff cloak has come up from Fenmere with a brown goat on a rope. Nobody has asked about the goat.
And there is the delegate from Merrowgate: Provost Elske Marrow, grey-eyed, ink on two fingers, with a guild clerk at her elbow who writes down everything, including the weather.

opening.text: Ashford will not sit below Merrowgate. Not on the first day. It sets a precedent.
Below? It's a table, Iona. It doesn't have a below.
It has a head, Reeve. Heads have a below.

opening.narrate: Sorrel, who has had the morning she was expecting, points at Orin.

opening.text: Stoneward. You're sergeant at arms. Keep order.
Understood.

opening.narrate: Orin takes the job the way he takes every job. Within the hour he has collected two belt knives, a letter-opener and the bread knife, which he returns to the cook with an apology and a receipt. He stops at the goat.

opening.text: Madam. Does she bite?
Only Ashford.

opening.narrate: At midday Elske Marrow takes the seating chart off the wall, turns it over and draws a circle. Order of arrival. Merrowgate, which arrived first, she puts last. It takes her five minutes, and nobody can find anything wrong with it, which annoys Iona more than the head of the table did.

opening.text: There. Now that the furniture is settled, Fenmere's delegate has something to say. She has been waiting since breakfast.
Since the day before yesterday. Fenmere sent for help three days ago. The mist is in our lower fields. This is the meeting I sent for.

opening.narrate: The council spends the afternoon on who should pay for it.

opening.text: Every one of them means what they say. That is the trouble.
Can't we just go? Fenmere's two days east. We could be halfway.
Without supplies or a road warrant. We'd arrive as six more mouths.

talks.label: Ask Provost Marrow why she gave Merrowgate the last seat

lines.narrate: Elske is on the wall walk, looking down at the refugee camp in the lower pass. She does not turn around.

lines.text: Because the last seat speaks last, and by then everyone is tired of talking. People mistake that for modesty.
You broke the Single Voice. Good. Corvane turned it into a fist. It was meant to be a hand.

lines.narrate: She says it the way people say the name of a house they used to live in.

lines.text: You knew its design.
I drew it, Sister. A long time ago, for a town that no longer exists. I'll tell you about it when there is time, and there is never time. That is rather my point.
She's telling the truth. All of it, as far as I can hear.

talks.label: Sit with Brannagh of Fenmere and her goat

lines.narrate: Brannagh has taken the rocking chair without complaint and is eating an apple in very small, very deliberate bites. The goat is eating the core of the last one.

lines.text: Sit down. You make the room look busy.

Fenmere has two halves. The upper village on the rise, the lower village by the water. The mist came into the lower fields four days ago. Our keeper says the ward will hold the lower village a week. Our keeper is an optimist. I've told her so.
What's the goat's name?
She's with me.

lines.narrate: That appears to be all the answer there is going to be.

lines.text: Get them to say yes to something before dark. Anything. Once a council has said yes once, it gets the taste for it.

talks.label: Ask Aveline how she is holding up

lines.text: Fine. Busy. I have the Briarwatch grain figures, the Briarwatch roof figures and a letter from Tovin asking whether his apprentice may ring the practice bell at night. The answer is no. I've written it three times.
When did you last sleep?
I slept on the cart.
You did the grain figures on the cart. I watched you.

lines.narrate: Aveline looks at her satchel as if it has betrayed her.

lines.text: When this council has agreed on one thing, Stoneward, I will sleep for a week. Help me get it there.

chairs.clue: Every delegate is waiting for someone else to pay first, because whoever pays for Fenmere today pays for every town tomorrow. Highpass's own ward can only ring at full strength with all five towns' consent: the charter you left at the beacon, or the custom of the independent keepers, makes it so.

investigate.label: Find out what is really stopping the vote

success.narrate: By late afternoon you can name the knot. Ashford will pay if Merrowgate pays. Merrowgate will pay if the money is a loan. Highpass will pay in soldiers, not coin, and has no soldiers to spare. Nobody is lying. Everybody is afraid of being the first.

success.text: Off the record? If I say yes today, my guild makes me pay for every washed-out bridge from here to the sea. I'll say yes. I need someone else to say it first.

investigate.failure: The arguments go round so many times you lose the thread, but you notice who is watching whom. Each delegate is waiting for someone else to commit first.

route.label: Take the cliff path down to the lower gate
route.success: You go down the cliff path instead of the switchbacks and reach the lower gate while the mist is still in the trees. The wardens on the gate have time to hear what you need from them.
route.failure: The switchbacks are jammed with people coming up and carts going down. You get to the lower gate bruised and late, as the first cold touches the palisade.

direct.label: Go down the switchbacks with everyone else
direct.text: You go down the switchbacks in the crush, with carts going down and people coming up, and reach the lower gate together, late, as the cold touches the palisade.

approach.narrate: The bell in the watchtower starts to ring the alarm just before sunset. Not the ward. The ordinary alarm, a hand-bell, swung by somebody who has run out of better ideas.

approach.text: Mist in the lower pass. It followed the Fenmere rider up the valley. The camp's below the line of the ward.

approach.narrate: The ward itself hangs in Highpass's gate arch, and it is answering the mist in a thin, uncertain voice. Since the beacon, no single keeper may ring it to full strength alone.

approach.text: Don't look at me like that. I'm coming.

crisis.narrate: The Gloam comes up the lower pass like a tide coming in over flat sand: quietly, faster than it looks. Where it touches the palisade the wood greys and goes soft, and the frost on it forms in the shapes of things that were there earlier: a cart, a fire, a child's hopscotch squares. Shapes come out of it with it. Not quite people. What the mist has taken, walking.

crisis.text: Wall's no good against that. The ward is.

crisis.narrate: Up in the gate arch the Highpass ward is ringing at a third of its strength. To ring it fully, the delegates who followed you down must say together that they consent. Elske is already beside the bell-rope. Iona is at the back, and Brannagh is between them with the goat.

crisis.text: This is what I meant. Five people must agree before a bell may ring. Tell them quickly.

peaceful.label: Get the five delegates to consent, here and now

success.text: Fenmere consents. I'd like it noted Fenmere consented first.
Ashford consents. Note that too.

success.narrate: Aveline, Sorrel and Elske say it together. The ward catches the five voices and rings with all of them, and the note goes down the pass like a wave pushing back the tide. The shapes in the mist come apart into frost, and the frost melts.

success.text: Agreed in under a minute. When the alternative is dying, councils are wonderfully efficient.

failure.text: I can't commit Ashford on a bell-rope. I need it in writing.

failure.narrate: The ward rings at half strength. It is not enough. The shapes come over the palisade, and you have to hold the gate while the delegates find their words.

objective.name: Hold the lower gate until the ward rings
objective.label: Hold the gate and give the delegates time
objective.description: Four successful actions hold the gate long enough for the five delegates to consent and the ward to ring at full strength.
objective.failText: The mist reaches the first tents before the ward rings. The people escape uphill; their tents, their bedding and some of what they remembered do not.
objective.successText: Five voices answer together. The ward rings at full strength and the pass clears from the top down.

after.narrate: Afterwards the council goes back up to the mess, where the chairs are exactly as they were. Somebody has found a sixth one.

after.text: Well. We agreed on something.
Well. We agreed on something.
We did. Can we agree on another thing before I fall over?
We did. Can we agree on another thing before I fall over?
Well. We didn't agree on anything, and we're all still alive. I'd like that noted.
Then let's agree on one thing before I fall over.

after.narrate: Elske Marrow stays standing.

after.text: Fenmere's help leaves at first light. It should have left three days ago. I'll say it once and then I'll stop: a council that needs a mist at the door to agree on anything will always agree one day late. When the council sits again, Merrowgate will make a proposal. I'd like you all to read it before you hate it.
She means that too.

after.narrate: Then the room argues, for the last time today, about who pays for Fenmere.

decisions.label: Back Brannagh: each town pays by what it has to lose

text.text: Big towns lose more, big towns pay more. My goat could work that out.

text.narrate: Iona does the sum, scowls, and signs. The council has its first agreement on paper. It took eleven hours and a mist.

decisions.label: Take Merrowgate's offer: the lantern guilds lend the money

text.narrate: Elske's clerk produces the loan papers before anyone has finished asking for them. They are generous, well drafted and signed in advance by Guildmaster Pell Haverick of the Merrowgate lantern guilds, who is not in the room.

text.text: Who's Haverick?
The man who pays for my lamps. He likes to be useful.

decisions.label: Pledge your contract fee to start Fenmere's relief tonight
decisions.description: This decision is permanent. The council repays your pledge from the relief fund once it is agreed, so your reward is unchanged; the story remembers who paid first.

text.narrate: You put your contract fee on the table, as a pledge, so the first carts can leave tonight. It is not enough for a week, but it is enough for a day, and the room goes very quiet.

text.text: That's not how councils work.
It is now. Ashford, you're embarrassed. Pay the rest.

text.narrate: Iona pays the rest. Later the relief fund pays back your pledge to the penny, and Iona sends you a receipt for it, very correctly made out, with a note on the back that just says: noted.

fenmere.name: Fenmere Under the Gloam
fenmere.region: Fenmere, two days east of Highpass
fenmere.threat: The Gloam has taken Fenmere's lower village and is climbing toward the upper village on the rise. Floodwater runs ahead of it. Bring light; a rope helps on the causeway.
fenmere.brief: The council's help reaches Fenmere a day late. The lower village is gone. Get its people up the rise and keep the upper village from going the same way.

opening.narrate: You come over the last fell at noon and see Fenmere the way the crows see it. The upper village sits on its rise, chimneys smoking. Below it, where Brannagh said the lower village would be, there is a white field, perfectly flat, perfectly still. The roofs are under it. There is no sound at all.

opening.text: That's the lower village.

opening.narrate: She says it the way she would say the name of a neighbour. Then she starts down the hill, and you have to hurry to keep up with a woman of seventy and her goat.

On the rise, the people of the lower village are sitting on their bundles in the churchyard: three hundred of them, give or take. They got out. They got out with what they could carry, two nights ago, while the council was arguing about chairs. Some of them are already looking at the white field as if they can't quite remember what was under it.

opening.text: That's the Gloam's work. It takes the warmth first, then the memory.
How long since the ward went quiet?
Since this morning. I'm the keeper. I was ringing it all night, and then I couldn't remember the third verse. I can't remember it now. I've known it since I was nine.

talks.label: Go with Brannagh to look at the lower village

lines.narrate: Brannagh stands at the edge of the white and looks at a place about a hundred yards in, where a weathervane sticks up out of the mist at a slant.

lines.text: That's my roof. Forty years. I re-thatched it in spring. Paid a man from Ashford, and he did it badly, and I made him do it again.

lines.narrate: She does not cry. She does not do anything. After a while the goat leans against her leg and she puts a hand on its head.

lines.text: Three days. If help had come in three days, the ward would have held. Ilka would still have her verse. Write that down somewhere, would you? Somebody should.

talks.label: Ask the lower-village families what the mist has taken from them

lines.narrate: A man knows his daughter's face but not her name. He keeps starting to say it. A woman remembers her house in every detail except which door was hers. A boy of about eight has forgotten he was afraid of the dark, and keeps walking toward the white field to see what's in it.

lines.text: It will come back to most of them, if the mist goes back down. Not all. Not all of it.
I've got him.

lines.narrate: Nessa has the boy by the back of his collar. She sits him down beside Biscuit and tells him the dog's whole history, most of it invented, and he stays.

fenmere.clue: Fenmere's ward is a song in four verses. Ilka has lost the third, but the villagers each remember a piece of it: the lower village sang it at weddings. Rung with the whole song, the ward can push the Gloam back off the rise, though not out of the lower village.

investigate.label: Help Ilka find the third verse among the villagers
investigate.success: An old woman remembers the first line. A fisherman remembers the tune and not the words. A girl of twelve, who was at her cousin's wedding in the spring, sings the whole thing through without stopping and then bursts into tears because she doesn't know why it's sad. Ilka writes it on her arm in charcoal.
investigate.failure: Between them, the villagers put back most of the verse. A girl of twelve, who heard it at her cousin's wedding in the spring, gets further than anyone, then stops at a line in the middle and cannot find it again. Ilka will have to fill it with something true and hope the ward accepts it.

route.label: Get the last families up the causeway before the water rises
route.success: You rope the causeway and bring the last carts up in a line, the sick riding, the rest walking. The water comes up behind the last cart and stops, as if disappointed.
route.failure: The causeway goes under while the last cart is on it. You get everyone off, but you are soaked and frozen and someone's grandfather has to be carried the last hundred yards on Orin's back.

approach.narrate: The Gloam always sends water ahead of itself. The fen drains are backing up, and the causeway between the lower fields and the rise is already ankle-deep. Two families are still down there, at the miller's house, because the miller will not leave his mill.

approach.text: We go now or we don't go.

crisis.narrate: At dusk the white field begins to climb the rise. It does not hurry. It takes the hedge at the bottom of the churchyard, and the hedge goes grey, and then it is a hedge-shaped piece of frost.

Things walk out of the mist: the shapes of what it took. A cart-horse made of cold. A woman who might have been someone's mother, carrying a basket of nothing. They do not attack, exactly. They come toward warmth, and wherever they touch, the warmth goes out.

crisis.text: I can ring it. I have the verse. I need someone between me and them until I've sung all four.
I can ring it. Three verses of it. The third's gone, and I've asked everyone I could find. I'll sing what I have, and I need someone between me and them while I try.
Then sing, girl. You've got a sergeant at arms.

crisis.narrate: Orin is already moving, shield up, to stand between the keeper and the white.

peaceful.label: Have the whole village sing the ward with Ilka

success.narrate: You get them on their feet: three hundred people who have lost their homes, standing in a churchyard in the dark. Ilka starts the first verse alone. By the second the fishermen have it. By the third, the twelve-year-old who knew it from her cousin's wedding is leading it, and nobody is ashamed to follow a child.

You get them on their feet: three hundred people who have lost their homes, standing in a churchyard in the dark. Ilka starts the first verse alone. By the second the fishermen have it. At the third she stops, and in the silence a girl of twelve at the back, who was at her cousin's wedding in the spring, starts singing it, very quietly. Nobody knew she knew it. By the end of the line the whole churchyard has it, and nobody is ashamed to follow a child.
The ward takes the song and rings it out, and the white field stops at the churchyard wall. Then, slowly, it goes back down the hill, a yard at a time, like a dog that has been told no.
It does not go back off the lower village. That is gone.

peaceful.failure: The song starts strong and falters at the missing line. The ward rings, but thinly, and the shapes keep coming. You will have to hold them back while Ilka finds the words.

objective.name: Ring Fenmere's ward through all four verses
objective.label: Keep the shapes off the keeper as she sings
objective.description: Four successful actions see Ilka through the four verses of the ward-song.
objective.failText: The mist takes the churchyard wall and the bottom row of houses on the rise before the song is finished. Their families are safe. Their houses are not.
objective.successText: The fourth verse rings out. The white field stops at the churchyard wall and begins to go back down the hill.

after.narrate: By morning the upper village is safe and the lower village is a white field with a weathervane sticking out of it. People begin, slowly, to remember. The man remembers his daughter's name and says it about forty times in a row. The boy remembers he is afraid of the dark, and is delighted.
Brannagh sits on the churchyard wall with her goat and looks at the white field.

after.text: Well. Now we have to decide what to do with three hundred people and no lower village. And I'll have to do it on my own, because the council is two days away and it'll take them a week.

decisions.label: Help them build again on the rise, above the old waterline

text.text: Sensible. Dull. Right. We'll build on the rise.

text.narrate: You spend two days helping mark out the new plots. Brannagh insists on the worst one for herself, the one that floods, because she says it will remind her of home.

decisions.label: Promise Brannagh the lower village will be taken back one day

text.text: Don't promise me things. I'm seventy.
Promise them.

text.narrate: She nods at the churchyard, where the families of the lower village are sorting what they carried out. You promise them. Orin watches you do it, and says nothing, and you know exactly what he thinks of promises.

southroad.name: The Long Road South
southroad.region: The south road from Briarwatch to Merrowgate
southroad.threat: Armed men are holding the south road and taking a toll in food. They are disciplined, they are hungry, and their sergeant does not want to be talked out of anything.
southroad.brief: The council will sit next at Merrowgate, where Provost Marrow will make her proposal. The south road is held by 'bandits'. Get the party, and Briarwatch's delegate, through to the harbour city.

opening.narrate: Briarwatch is the same, and it isn't. The bell rings the hours. The square has been swept. There are new houses on the Ashford road, built by people who arrived with nothing after the beacon and decided this was as good a place as any.
Smith Dera has your gear on the bench before you have finished saying hello.

opening.text: Fenmere. I heard. Everybody's heard. Is it true the old woman has a goat?
Yes.
What's the goat for?
Nobody knows.
That's worth a free strap. Go on.

opening.narrate: Tovin is at the bell tower with his apprentice, Pim, who is fourteen and has read every book on bell-keeping in Briarwatch, both of them, several times.

opening.text: Is it true the Gloam took the lower village in Fenmere because the council was late? Because I've been thinking, if the bell had been rung every hour, on the hour, the whole time—
Pim. Breathe.
Sorry. I just think about it a lot.
So do I. That's why I'm teaching you to breathe first.

opening.narrate: Aveline is coming with you to Merrowgate. She has packed one bag of clothes and three bags of papers. Then, at the guildhouse, the news that matters: the south road has been closed for a fortnight. A band of armed men holds the old checkpoint at Kell's Bridge and takes a toll in food. Carts that pay go through. Carts that don't, don't.

talks.label: Ask Orin why he's gone quiet since he heard about the checkpoint

lines.narrate: Orin is checking the buckles on his shield, which he checked an hour ago.

lines.text: Kell's Bridge was a beacon station. Under the Single Voice. Soldiers crewed it, rang the echo-stones when Central Command told them to.
When you broke the Single Voice, nobody told the crews. Nobody paid them, either. Some of them had been out there two years.
I knew a few of them. Hal took a commission with Central Command after the bridge. She wrote to me. I didn't write back.
If it's them, I want to be the one at the front.

talks.label: Help Aveline carry her papers

lines.text: Careful with that one. That's Briarwatch's position on Provost Marrow's proposal.
You haven't read her proposal. Nobody has.
That's why it's three bags. One for if it's good, one for if it's bad, one for if it's good and I still don't trust her.
Which one do you expect to use?
Ask me when I've slept.

southroad.clue: The 'bandits' at Kell's Bridge are the crew of the old Single Voice beacon station, and others like them, led by Lieutenant Hal. They have not been paid since the beacon fell. A guild agent from Merrowgate has offered them work, on terms that would make them Merrowgate's army.

investigate.label: Talk to the carters who were turned back at Kell's Bridge

success.narrate: The carters were turned back politely. That's the first odd thing. The second is that the bandits took food but not money, and the third is that they gave receipts.

success.text: Receipts. That's Hal. She'd requisition a meal from her own mother and give her a receipt.

success.narrate: One of the carters adds that a man in a fine coat from Merrowgate went through the checkpoint two days ago, toll-free, and was invited in for supper.

investigate.failure: The carters are angry and not much use, but one of them kept the receipt the bandits gave him for a sack of oats. It is signed with a lieutenant's mark you have seen before, on Orin's letters.

route.label: Talk your way past the outer checkpoint

success.narrate: The plan is that you are traders. The plan lasts until the old soldier on the outer post looks at Orin.

success.text: Traders, are you? What are you trading?
We're not traders.

success.narrate: There is a short, terrible silence. Then Orin, who cannot leave a thing alone once he has seen it, points at the gate.

success.text: Your hinge is on the wrong side. Any cart that hits it swings it into your own men. Who hung it?
I did.
It's wrong.

success.narrate: The old soldier looks at the hinge. Then at Orin. Then at the hinge again, and you watch him recognise something that has nothing to do with gates.

success.text: Third Company?
Second.
Go on, then. Before you fix it. The lieutenant's at the bridge.

failure.narrate: The plan is that you are traders. Orin says, very clearly, that you are not traders. It does not go well after that. Somebody blows a whistle, and you arrive at the bridge with a dozen armed soldiers walking beside you, carefully not quite pointing anything at you.

approach.narrate: The road drops toward Kell's Bridge through a cutting. The old beacon station stands on the far bank: a squat tower with an iron frame on top, where the echo-stones used to hang. Somebody has planted cabbages around its base.
A wooden checkpoint closes the near end of the road. One soldier on it, old, with a crossbow he isn't holding properly because his hands are cold.

approach.text: We could go round. Through the gully.

crisis.narrate: Lieutenant Hal meets you on the bridge. She is thinner than when you saw her last, at the Ashford span, and her coat has been mended in three colours. Behind her are perhaps forty soldiers, some with families, all of them watching Orin.

crisis.text: Stoneward.
Hal.

You broke the Voice. Good. It needed breaking. And then you all went home, and nobody came out here to tell us it was finished. We heard from a carter. We've been eating the station's seed corn since the spring.

crisis.narrate: At her shoulder is a man in a very good coat: a Merrowgate guild agent, with a contract in a leather case.

crisis.text: Guildmaster Haverick offers the lieutenant's company a contract as harbour wardens. Pay, quarters, a pension. That offer closes at sundown. I'm sure the Briarwatch delegation wouldn't want to stand in the way of honest work.

crisis.narrate: But not all of Hal's soldiers are waiting for sundown. A sergeant called Brask, a big man with a burn up one side of his face, has his people drawn up across the end of the bridge.

crisis.text: We don't need the guild and we don't need the council. We've got the road. Whoever wants it can pay us for it.

peaceful.label: Make the soldiers an honest offer, and let Orin say it

success.narrate: You make the offer. Then you step back and let Orin say the rest, because he can only say what's true.

success.text: I don't know if the council will pay you. I think it will. It took them eleven hours to agree on a chair. But I'll be there when they decide, and I'll stand up and say what you did out here, and I won't lie about any of it. That's all I've got.

success.narrate: It turns out that is a great deal. Brask's line breaks up man by man, and the last to go is Brask himself, who says something short and rude to Orin and then shakes his hand.

success.text: You haven't changed, Stoneward. Still can't lie to save your life.
It's saved mine a few times.

failure.narrate: Brask's people come off the end of the bridge. Hal shouts at them to stand down; half of them do. The other half do not.

objective.name: Hold the bridge without a massacre
objective.label: Push the sergeant's line back without killing anyone
objective.description: Three successful actions break Brask's line so Hal can take her company back without a slaughter.
objective.failText: The fight spreads to the station. People are hurt on both sides, and some of Hal's soldiers will remember who hurt them.
objective.successText: Brask's line breaks. Hal walks into the middle of what is left of it and starts giving orders, and people start obeying them.

after.narrate: By evening the bridge is quiet, and the cabbages have survived. Hal's company eats supper with you in the yard of the beacon station. Aveline sits with Hal for an hour with her bags of papers open and comes back with an expression you have not seen on her before; it might be hope, or it might be lack of sleep.
The guild agent is waiting by his horse with his contract. Sundown has come and gone, and he has not left.

after.text: So. Council or guild. You brought us the offer, so you can tell me straight. Which would you take?

decisions.label: Ask Hal's company to keep the roads for the council

text.text: Road wardens for the council, then. Assuming the council pays.
Briarwatch will put it in writing. I have a bag for it.

text.narrate: The guild agent rides off toward Merrowgate. Hal watches him go.

text.text: He'll be back with a better offer. They always are.

decisions.label: Tell Hal to take the guild's contract; her people need paying now

text.text: Honest. I'll take it, then. Pension's real money. The council's money is a promise.

text.narrate: She signs. The guild agent shakes her hand with real warmth. Orin says nothing all evening, until the yard has gone quiet, and then only one thing.

text.text: She'll be Merrowgate's soldiers now. Remember that when the vote comes.

harbour.name: The Harbour Bell
harbour.threat: The lantern guilds are auctioning the harbour ward. Ashford's delegate, who meant to bid for the council, has gone missing on the night of the sale. Guild bravos guard the lantern-works; a rope or climbing kit opens the roofs.
harbour.brief: Merrowgate's guilds are selling the harbour bell to the highest bidder. The council means to bid, but Quartermaster Iona, who holds the council's purse, has vanished. Find her before the hammer falls.

opening.narrate: Merrowgate is built up the sides of a bay like seats in a theatre, and every seat has a lamp. The lamps are the lantern guilds'. So is the oil, the wick, the glass, and the right to light them, and a city ordinance makes it a crime to complain about the price after dark.
At your inn there is a letter waiting. It is from Quartermaster Iona, and it is an invoice.

opening.text: 'To repairs, Ashford span, following the hero's intervention: ninety-one crowns. To one cart, mislaid by the hero's party: four crowns. To refreshment of the hero's party at the quartermaster's expense, the night after: two crowns, eleven pence.' She's itemised the beer.
We did drink the beer.
Underneath she's written: 'Payment not expected. Recorded for the council's information. Settle at the harbour sale, where we will talk about something more important. I.'

opening.narrate: The something more important is posted on every door in the city. The harbour ward, the great bell in the tower on the mole that has kept the Gloam off the water for two hundred years, is to be sold at public auction tomorrow night by the Lantern Guilds of Merrowgate, its lawful owners. Bidding opens at ten thousand crowns.

opening.text: They're selling the harbour. You can't sell a harbour.
You can sell anything if nobody stops you at the door.

opening.narrate: The council's plan, agreed by letter over a week of argument, is that Iona will bid for all five towns with the council's purse, so that the harbour bell belongs to everyone. It is a good plan. It has one weakness, which becomes clear the next morning, when Iona does not come down to breakfast.

talks.label: Call on Guildmaster Pell Haverick at the Lantern Hall

lines.narrate: Pell Haverick receives you in a room lit by forty lamps, all burning, at noon. He is a round, kind-faced man with very clean hands, and he is delighted to meet you. He has been delighted to meet a great many people.

lines.text: The hero of the beacon! Sit, sit. I have read all about you. You broke a terrible machine, and now the towns have no machine at all, and the Gloam is in Fenmere. Somebody has to keep the lamps lit, don't they?
The sale is perfectly lawful. Bells are expensive. Whoever owns the harbour bell will have to pay to ring it. Better that they can afford to.
Where's the quartermaster from Ashford?
Is she missing? How dreadful. Merrowgate can be confusing for visitors. So many streets.
He's lying. Not about the streets.

talks.label: Find Provost Marrow and ask why she allows the sale

lines.text: Allow it? I've written against it four times. The guilds own the bell. They bought it from the city a hundred years ago, when the city was broke. It's lawful. Most terrible things are.
That is what a Warden would be for. Someone the council chose, who could say: not tonight. This bell is not for sale while the Gloam is on the water. And be removed afterwards if they were wrong.
You're going to propose it tomorrow, aren't you. At the sale.
In front of the whole city. Yes. I'd rather ask for power in daylight than take it at night, Reeve. Someone has already tried it the other way.

talks.label: Speak to the guild clerk with the limp on the north quay

lines.narrate: On the north quay a woman in a Lantern Guild coat is checking carters' passes against a list. You know the limp before you know the face. It is Lysa, the lookout from the Briarwood, who told you the truth about Sable and then walked away into the fern.

lines.text: Don't. I'm working.
You testified. At the hearing. I heard about it.

I testified. And afterwards nobody would hire a woman who'd been in the cult, except the people who don't ask where anyone has been. The guild doesn't ask. It pays on time, which is more than Sable ever did.

lines.narrate: She looks at her list for a long moment, and then, without looking up, at the old glass store at the end of the quay.

lines.text: They brought someone in through the back of the lantern-works last night. A small woman, complaining about breakfast. I didn't see it. I'm only telling you because you let me live, and it turns out I'd like to have been worth it.
The bell remembers who betrayed it. So do I. Go on, before somebody sees me talking to you.

talks.label: Find Hal among the harbour wardens

lines.narrate: Hal is on the quay in a new guild coat with brass buttons. She does not look at you as you come up, and she keeps her voice low.

lines.text: Lantern-works. The old glass store on the north quay. They took her through the back last night. I didn't see it, and I'm not telling you.
Thank you.
Don't. The pension's real. So's this. I'll work out which matters more later.

talks.label: Ask Hal's road wardens what they saw on the way in

lines.text: My lads brought the Ashford woman's coach in two nights ago. Her driver was paid off at the north gate by a man in a lantern-guild coat. Paid well. Driver bought a round for the whole guardhouse, which is how we know.
North gate. North quay's that way.
So's the lantern-works.

harbour.clue: The auction's rules disqualify any bidder whose named delegate is not in the hall when the hammer falls. With Iona gone, the council cannot bid, and every other bidder is a guild front. She was taken to the lantern-works on the north quay.

investigate.label: Read the auction rules, all of them

success.narrate: The rules run to eleven pages. Every one of them makes somebody richer. Bids are in guild scrip, bought from the guild at a premium. The auctioneer's fee is a share of the price. The winning bidder must buy the guild's oil for the bell for twenty years. And rule nine: a bidder whose named delegate is not in the hall when the hammer falls forfeits the bid, and the deposit.

success.text: So if Iona isn't there, the council doesn't just lose. It pays.
Who'd want her gone that badly?
Everyone else bidding.

investigate.failure: The rules are eleven pages of very small print, and you lose the thread twice. But you find rule nine, and that is the one that matters: no delegate at the hammer, no bid.

route.label: Go over the lantern-works roofs to the glass store
route.success: You go up a drainpipe and over the lantern-works' roofs, between the chimneys of the glass furnaces, and come down through a skylight into the store. Nobody looks up. People in Merrowgate never look up; the lamps are all at eye level.
route.failure: A slate goes from under your foot and down into the yard, and every guild bravo in the lantern-works looks up at once.

approach.narrate: The lantern-works fills a whole block of the north quay: furnaces, glass-cutters' sheds, a long store where finished lamps hang in rows like fruit. The front gate has four guild bravos on it and a bell-pull marked 'Deliveries'.

crisis.narrate: Iona is in the glass store, tied to a chair, which she seems to find more insulting than frightening. A man called Master Coyle, who fixes things for Guildmaster Haverick, is sitting opposite her with a pocket-watch open on his knee.

crisis.text: Ah. Good. You've had my letter. I was abducted on my way to breakfast, which I'd like noted, because I had paid for breakfast.

Nobody's been hurt. Nobody needs to be. The quartermaster stays here until the hammer falls at nine, then she goes home with a very nice apology from the guild. Or you make this difficult, and it's a long way down to the harbour.

crisis.narrate: Across the city, the bells strike eight. The auction hall is a quarter of an hour away by the quays, if the quays are clear. They are not clear: Coyle's people are already in the doorway.

peaceful.label: Show Coyle he's already lost, and walk Iona out

success.narrate: You tell Coyle the truth: half the council knows where you are, the city will hear about this before the hammer falls whether Iona is there or not, and Haverick will need someone to blame. You ask him who he thinks that will be.
Coyle closes his pocket-watch. He is a professional, and professionals know when a job has stopped paying.

success.text: I was never here.
You were. I've written it down.

failure.narrate: The bravos come in, and the glass store is the worst possible place for it. Lamps start to fall.

objective.name: Get Iona to the auction hall before the hammer falls
objective.label: Get the quartermaster out and across the quays
objective.description: Three successful actions get Iona out of the lantern-works and across the quays to the hall before nine.
objective.failText: You reach the hall as the hammer is raised. Iona shouts her bid from the doorway; it is accepted, barely, and only because half the hall is on her side by now. The guild will contest it for a year.
objective.successText: Iona walks into the auction hall at five to nine, with rope marks on her wrists and her invoice book under her arm.

after.narrate: On the north quay, a Lantern Guild coat is folded over a bollard, with a pass-list weighted down on top of it by a stone. Nobody in the guild seems to know where the clerk who wore it has gone. You have an idea she is somewhere she chose.
The auction hall goes quiet when Iona comes in. She sits down in the council's chair, straightens her cuffs, and raises her card.
Then, before the auctioneer can take the bid, Provost Elske Marrow stands up at the back of the hall, and the whole room turns round, because people always do when Elske stands up.

after.text: Before anyone buys the harbour, I have something to say to the council, and I would like Merrowgate to hear it.

A bell should not be sold. It should not wait for five towns to finish a letter, either. Fenmere waited. You all know what it cost. I propose a Warden of the Chorus: one person, chosen by the council, with emergency command of every ward for one year. Recallable at any time by two-thirds of the council. Named, public, answerable. Not a machine. A person you can sack.
I'll put it to the council before the winter, in the open. Until then, I ask that this sale be withdrawn. I can't make it be. That's rather my point.

after.narrate: Nobody says anything for a long time. Then the hall starts talking all at once, and does not stop until well after midnight.

after.text: Every word true.
That's what bothers me.

after.narrate: In the end the auctioneer, who has a share of the price and can count a room, asks the council what it wants done with the bell.

decisions.label: Let Iona's bid stand: the harbour bell belongs to the council

text.narrate: The hammer falls on Iona's card. The harbour bell belongs to five towns now, which means that ringing it will require five towns to agree.

text.text: I'd like that noted as a success. Also, the council owes me for breakfast.

decisions.label: Ask that the bell go to the harbour's own keepers, the fishers and pilots

text.narrate: It is not in the rules, but by now nobody in the hall cares about the rules. The fishers' and pilots' guild, who ring the bell every night and have never owned it, are given it for one crown, which Brannagh pays.

text.text: Fenmere wants it noted that it bought a harbour.

decisions.label: Name Haverick in front of the hall for the kidnapping

text.narrate: You tell the hall what happened to Iona and who Master Coyle works for. Haverick is not there. He is never there. By morning the guilds have issued a statement deploring the regrettable private conduct of a former employee, and the sale has been 'postponed'.

text.text: You've made him an enemy. And you've done me a favour I didn't ask for. Thank you, I think.

keeper.name: The Last Name on the List
